title: Kanaka Mahal festive branch banners: neutralize seven mixed-light premises heroes to an in-frame grey card, recolor one drape to the house maroon, triage-prep the crest and the foil seal, then data-merge one press-ready large-format banner per branch

source.reference: traditional Tamil festive large-format promotional banner set (multi-piece)

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief for a traditional South-Indian service business rolling out a festive promotional banner set in a regional (Tamil) script, and laundered to a fictional brand, 'Kanaka Mahal' (a fictional traditional catering & events hall) — no real company, person, place, festival, or trademark is named; branch localities and the 'Maalai Vizha' festival-season label are invented. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original brief is a from-scratch DESIGN + regional-script TYPESETTING + multi-size LAYOUT job, all out of connector scope, and the earlier rebuild of this slot exported six authored .ai masters that carried EMPTY placeholder frames — nothing in the connector can PLACE a hero photo, a logo, or a texture into an .ai (document_render_vector only exports), so the graded hero, the vector crest, and the halftone motif were orphaned with no path onto the printed banner. The corrected design gives the client a genuinely hand-authored InDesign SINGLE-RECORD banner template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> AND FOUR @-prefixed image-path columns, so every chain-produced asset reaches the layout as a MERGE BIND rather than banned free-form placement: @Hero (the branch's graded premises photo, distinct per row), @Crest (the shared vectorized brand crest), @Seal (the shared photographed gold-foil premises seal kept as transparent raster), and @Texture (the shared screen-print halftone motif derived from a graded hero). document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW, so a per-BRANCH single-record banner is the correct, connector-doable shape (the branch is the variable dimension); a single .indd template holds one page size, so true multi-physical-size output is the large-format printer's RIP job and is NOT claimed here. The client supplies the authored .indd, the branch roster CSV, seven raw premises hero photos shot at each branch under mismatched festival lighting each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame, a flat solid-fill brand crest, a photograph of the embossed gold-foil premises seal, and last year's flattened proof PDF for reuse. The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralize every hero to its own in-frame grey card so the whole banner series shares one white point, recolor one branch's bright-red decor drape to the deep-maroon house colour without a reshoot, derive a traditional screen-print halftone motif, triage the crest vs the foil seal so each is prepped the correct way, back-convert last year's proof to an editable source, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export a press-ready banner per branch.
one_line_ask: Neutralize seven mixed-lighting branch premises photos to the 18% grey card each one carries so the festive banner series reads as one matched set, decide per frame how far to move white balance without killing any branch's genuine festival colour, recolor one branch's bright-red drape to the deep-maroon house colour without reshooting, derive a screen-print halftone motif, prep the crest and the foil seal each the correct way for print, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign banner template against the branch roster to produce one press-ready large-format banner per branch.
full_brief: Kanaka Mahal is a traditional catering & events hall and we are running our Maalai Vizha festive-season promotion across seven branches — one large-format vinyl banner per branch, each printed at 12 ft x 6 ft and read from across a busy street, so it has to look rich, warm and unmistakably from one brand. Our banner LAYOUT and the festive headline are already signed off and locked: the headline is set in a licensed regional-script display font as fixed artwork in our InDesign template — do NOT re-typeset, re-translate, or touch that type, because the spelling has been proofed and any edit risks corrupting the script. What we need is the production, and we are handing you everything the job needs. First, the premises photos: seven shots, one of each branch's decorated frontage/stage, but here is the problem — they were taken by different branch managers on different evenings under whatever festival lighting was up (some under warm tungsten string-lights, some under cool white LED wash, one under greenish work-lights and dim, one badly over-exposed against the evening sky, one strong blue open-shade), so straight out of the folder they look like seven unrelated pictures. A banner series where every branch has a different colour cast looks cheap and off-brand. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into a corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every image to one consistent, true-to-life festive look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole series shares one white point and one warmth. Do NOT force one blanket correction across all seven: each was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target — some frames need warming, some need cooling, one is a colour problem on a second axis, one needs its blown highlights pulled back first. Be careful: at least one branch's frontage is genuinely, deeply gold — real brass lamps and marigold under warm-but-neutral light — and if its grey card already reads neutral you must NOT 'cool a blue cast' that isn't there or you will strip the exact festive colour we are selling. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame AND the final pixel size of each hero crop, so we can confirm the set is matched and that every banner will hold up at print size: each hero drops into a large hero window on the 12 x 6 ft banner and at our large-format print resolution that window needs at least ~4320 x 2160 px of real image — a photo cropped down small will print soft and pixelated across a 12-foot banner, which we will reject, and we do not accept any upscaling to fake it. Second, a colour fix without a reshoot: on the branch whose entrance is draped in a bright pillar-box RED cloth, give us a version where that drape is our deep-maroon house colour instead (a rich, dark maroon/burgundy in the SAME warm-red family, just deepened and muted — not a jump to a far-off hue), and the recolour has to sit under the real folds, sheen and shadow of the cloth, touching ONLY the drape — no flat dead colour, no whole-image tint bleeding onto the lamps and people. Third, a traditional touch: derive a screen-print / halftone texture motif from one of the graded heroes so the banner carries a printed-poster feel up close; it drops into a fixed texture panel in our layout. Fourth, the brand marks: we are giving you two logo files — our flat two-colour crest, and a close-up PHOTOGRAPH of the embossed gold-foil seal from our premises signboard. Prep both so they drop cleanly into the banner and stay sharp at print size — but they are NOT the same kind of file and must not be treated the same way; think about which one can honestly become clean line art and which one would be destroyed by that. Fifth, we still have last year's banner only as a flattened proof PDF — convert it back into an editable InDesign source so we can reuse the frame next year. Finally, build the banners: we have hand-built the InDesign banner template with the real placeholder fields and the image slots (hero, crest, foil seal, and texture panel), and we are giving you the branch roster; merge them so every branch gets its own single banner with its name, address, phone, offer line and valid dates bound in, its graded hero dropped into the hero window, the crisp crest and the foil seal in their windows, and the halftone motif in the texture panel — then hand back a press-ready banner per branch. Bind the branch copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our addresses, offers or dates. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole series on one white point while the genuinely-gold branch keeps its real colour; every hero crop at least ~4320 x 2160 px with no upscaling; the drape recolour natural under the existing light and confined to the cloth; the crest a clean vector and the foil seal a sharp raster that still looks like foil; and exactly one press-ready banner per roster row.

inputs.name: kanaka_mahal_banner_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD large-format festive promotional banner — ONE branch per page — authored at a proportional design scale of a 12 ft x 6 ft (2:1 landscape) vinyl banner with 1-inch full-scale bleed on all sides and CMYK intent, targeting ~72 DPI effective at full 12 x 6 ft size (standard for a distance-viewed large-format banner). It must contain: the locked festive headline and the maroon/gold ornamental frame already set as FIXED artwork (the headline typeset in a licensed regional-script display OpenType font as real, proofed text — never to be re-typeset by the connector); live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<BranchName>>, <<Address>>, <<Phone>>, <<OfferLine>>, <<ValidDates>>; and FOUR @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to four separate image frames — a large 2:1 hero window bound to @Hero (the branch's graded premises photo), a corner crest window bound to @Crest (the vectorized brand crest), a small seal accent window bound to @Seal (the transparent-ground foil seal raster), and a side texture panel bound to @Texture (the halftone motif). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, EVERY per-image asset reaches the banner ONLY as a merge bind through these four image frames — nothing is dropped in by hand. The <<BranchName>> and <<Address>> frames have Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so longer branch copy binds without going overset. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and all four image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (a converted-PDF template has no live merge fields and no data-merge image field, so it would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one branch's worth of fields).
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a per-branch single-record banner is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. FOUR image columns (@Hero, @Crest, @Seal, @Texture) mean the merge resolves four prepped assets per row and gives every chain-produced asset (the branch hero, the vector crest, the foil seal, the halftone motif) a real connector-doable path onto the banner without any free-form placement — this is exactly what heals the killed design's empty-placeholder-frame defect. The locked headline stays fixed template artwork so the connector never re-typesets the proofed regional script (protecting the brief's 'no spelling errors' acceptance). Column names must exactly match the roster headers.

inputs.name: kanaka_branch_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: BranchName,Address,Phone,OfferLine,ValidDates,@Hero,@Crest,@Seal,@Texture and 7 branch rows for the fictional 'Kanaka Mahal' catering & events hall, one per branch. BranchName is an invented locality label (e.g. 'Kanaka Mahal - Amaravathi Nagar', 'Kanaka Mahal - Ponni Street', 'Kanaka Mahal - Maruthur', 'Kanaka Mahal - Vaigai Nagar', 'Kanaka Mahal - Sengalam Road', 'Kanaka Mahal - Thoranam Junction', 'Kanaka Mahal - Kambar Salai') with at least two deliberately long names so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. Address is a fictional multi-line street address; Phone a fictional local number; OfferLine a short festive-promotion line (e.g. 'Maalai Vizha season: 20% off hall bookings'); ValidDates a date range. The @Hero column holds the branch's prepped hero filename (hero_b1_final.jpg ... hero_b7_final.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct graded premises photo into that banner. @Crest holds the SAME vectorized crest file (brand_crest.svg) in EVERY row; @Seal holds the SAME transparent foil-seal file (foil_seal_transparent.png) in EVERY row; @Texture holds the SAME halftone motif file (halftone_texture_motif.png) in EVERY row — so the three shared marks land on every branch's banner as merge binds. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<BranchName>>,<<Address>>,<<Phone>>,<<OfferLine>>,<<ValidDates>> and the four @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Seven rows => the merge must produce exactly seven finished banners (page-count = row-count gate). @Hero is per-branch (distinct filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency), while @Crest / @Seal / @Texture carry the identical shared filename in all seven rows so the vector crest, the foil seal, and the halftone motif each reach every banner via the merge — the only connector-doable path since free-form placement is banned (mirrors AO-74/AO-75's multi-image-column pattern). Long branch names exercise the auto-fit frame. All branch copy binds verbatim; nothing is rewritten.

inputs.name: raw_branch_heroes_x7.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 7 photoreal wide LANDSCAPE (roughly 3:2, ~5400-6000 px on the long edge — full-resolution stills straight off a 24MP camera) photographs, each of a different decorated South-Indian catering/events-hall FRONTAGE or festive stage at night, each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference. Shot on different evenings under mismatched festival light so no single correction fits: (1) warm tungsten string-lights over a marigold-garlanded entrance, frame tilted ~4 deg; (2) cool white LED wash on a draped stage, level; (3) greenish work-light cast over a side entrance AND dim/underexposed, tilted ~3 deg; (4) mixed warm+cool light on an entrance draped in a BRIGHT PILLAR-BOX RED cloth with brass lamps, level (this is the drape-recolor hero); (5) badly OVER-exposed against a bright evening sky, blown highlights on a white pandal roof, level; (6) a genuinely DEEP-GOLD frontage — real brass kuthuvilakku lamps and dense marigold under warm-but-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the real decor, not a white-balance error), level; (7) strong cool BLUE open-shade cast on a courtyard, AND dark/underexposed, tilted ~4 deg. Every shot has real garland/fabric/brass texture, candid documentary feel, cluttered festive surroundings, no studio gloss, no CGI; the grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in every frame.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA-scale capture at ~5400-6000 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each 2:1 hero crop can fill the banner hero window at >=4320 x 2160 px by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure, tilt vary in OPPOSITE directions) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision measured to its in-frame 18% grey card, the free checkable neutral target. Frame 6 is the TRAP: its warmth is real festive decor and its card is already neutral, so cooling it is wrong. Frame 4 carries the bright-red drape for the masked recolor. Delivered as a zip of 7 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs; the grey card is cropped out for the final banner but retained on the neutralized master for grading.

inputs.name: brand_crest_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat, slightly low-resolution raster brand crest for 'Kanaka Mahal': a circular emblem with a stylised brass oil-lamp (kuthuvilakku) motif and a small lotus underline, in solid maroon and gold on a plain white background, exported slightly oversized and off-centre with a thin white margin. Crisp solid colour fills, no gradients, no photographic texture, hard clean edges — the kind of logo that vectorizes cleanly — but rendered at modest resolution so visible pixel/edge stair-stepping is present.
inputs.realism_notes: Solid-fill, limited-palette, hard-edged emblem is the correct candidate for image_vectorize after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds + crisp). Mild aliasing makes the vectorize a genuine cleanup, not a no-op. This is one of the two brand marks — the one that CAN honestly become clean vector line art (@Crest).

inputs.name: foil_seal_photo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of the embossed GOLD-FOIL 'Kanaka Mahal' premises seal from a signboard, shot on a dark surface: shiny metallic gold foil with specular highlights, soft reflections, raised-emboss shadowing, subtle surface texture and smooth tonal gradients across the lamp emblem and lettering. Clearly a photographed glossy metallic object, ~2000 px, full of gradients and sheen — NOT flat line art.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRIAGE / TRAP asset. It looks like 'just another logo file', but it is a photographed metallic foil surface full of gradients and specular sheen: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy silhouette that destroys the foil look. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency -> keep as a high-resolution RASTER placed via @Seal. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the seal prints flat and dead across a 12-foot banner. Distinct from brand_crest_flat.png precisely so the two superficially-similar 'logo' inputs need DIFFERENT correct treatments.

inputs.name: last_year_proof.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: A single-page, flattened, export-style landscape PDF proof of last year's Kanaka Mahal festive banner: a maroon/gold ornamental frame, a regional-script festive headline, a photo block, the circular kuthuvilakku crest, and a branch/offer line — with NO live editable layers (a flat rendered proof). Fictional brand only; no other business name.
inputs.realism_notes: Feeds document_convert_pdf (PDF -> genuine editable .indd) as a reuse deliverable. A flattened proof is exactly the realistic input for that back-conversion the client requested. It is NOT used as a merge target (convert_pdf_to_indd output cannot bind merge fields) — the merge runs against the separately hand-authored kanaka_mahal_banner_template.indd.

outputs.name: KanakaMahal_BranchBanners_x7.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly seven press-ready large-format festive banners — ONE single-record banner per roster row (page-count = row-count = 7) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge, each authored at the 12 ft x 6 ft (2:1) design scale with 1-inch full-scale bleed and CMYK intent, ~72 DPI effective at full size. Each banner binds its BranchName/Address/Phone/OfferLine/ValidDates verbatim from the roster; drops that branch's grey-card-neutralized hero into the 2:1 hero window (via @Hero, >=4320 x 2160 px so it prints sharp at 12 ft); and drops the shared vectorized crest (@Crest), the transparent-ground foil seal (@Seal), and the halftone motif (@Texture) into their windows — all four by merge bind, never free-form placement. The locked regional-script headline is untouched fixed artwork on every page.

outputs.name: branch_heroes_graded_x7
outputs.spec: Seven grey-card-neutralized, straightened branch hero photos, delivered as the hero-window 2:1 crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while holding a warm festive tone, and true-to-decor (the genuinely-gold branch's real colour NOT forced off); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered 2:1 hero crop (the *_final output that binds into that branch's banner) — framed on the frontage with the grey card fully cropped OUT and at >=4320 x 2160 px. The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop; the pixel floor is never evaluated on the card-bearing master. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance/exposure move AND the final pixel dimensions of each hero.

outputs.name: variant_b4_drape_maroon.jpg
outputs.spec: Recolored variant of the branch-4 hero: the bright pillar-box RED entrance drape deepened to the Kanaka Mahal house maroon via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge toward wine plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the red — an in-band adjacent shift, NOT a near-complementary rotation), riding the drape's existing luminosity so its folds, sheen highlights and cast shadow stay natural and the brass lamps, people and surroundings are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat dead-fill. This is the hero that binds into the branch-4 banner (@Hero for that row).

outputs.name: brand_crest.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the flat brand crest, traced only after the raster is crop-to-bounds-tightened and crisped, razor-sharp at the banner crest window with solid maroon/gold fills and no captured white margin — bound into every banner via @Crest.

outputs.name: foil_seal_transparent.png
outputs.spec: The photographed gold-foil premises seal cropped to bounds and knocked to transparency then kept as a high-resolution RASTER (>=1296 px square so it prints sharp in the seal window) — deliberately NOT vectorized, so the metallic foil sheen and emboss survive to print. Bound into every banner via @Seal. This is the triage-correct counterpart to brand_crest.svg.

outputs.name: halftone_texture_motif.png
outputs.spec: A traditional screen-print / halftone texture motif derived from a graded hero via image_apply_halftone, resized to the banner's texture-panel window for the close-up printed-poster aesthetic. High-res PNG, bound into every banner via @Texture.

outputs.name: last_year_editable.indd
outputs.spec: Last year's flattened proof PDF back-converted to a genuine editable InDesign source (document_convert_pdf) so the client can reuse the frame next season. A standalone reuse deliverable — NOT used as the merge template (convert_pdf_to_indd output cannot bind merge fields).

connector_workflow.note: Triage: branch-1 is tilted ~4 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames 1/3/7 get straightened; the level frames 2/4/5/6 skip this — deciding which is part of the job.)

Warm tungsten string-light cast: COOL it (negative temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and hold a warm festive tone. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _vibrance_and_saturation / _brightness_and_contrast).

Crop the neutralized frame to the 2:1 banner hero window, framing on the frontage with the grey card cropped OUT, keeping the result at >=4320 x 2160 px so it clears the large-format print floor. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand. The pre-crop b1_neutralized (card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion + px floor are the separate checks on this crop. Report final px.

Level frame, cool white LED wash: WARM it (positive temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point established on frame 1 — the OPPOSITE direction from frame 1, proving a blanket pass fails. Set exposure to match set brightness. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 2:1 hero window at >=4320 x 2160 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. (This graded hero also feeds the halftone motif at step 21.)
Branch-3 is tilted ~3 deg — level it before grading.

Greenish work-light cast AND underexposed: the dominant colour move is on TINT (push toward magenta) to kill the green while neutralizing the grey card, PLUS a real exposure lift — a two-axis problem, not a simple temperature slide. Land the card neutral on the shared white point. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 2:1 hero window at >=4320 x 2160 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Branch-4 (level), mixed warm+cool light: neutralize its grey card to the shared white point (a modest correction). This neutralized full-res frame feeds BOTH the drape-recolor branch AND the final crop, so keep it full-res before cropping. Its grey card is graded here for neutrality; the bright-red drape stays red in this master. Report the move.

On the neutralized branch-4 hero, semantically select ONLY the bright-red entrance drape cloth ('the bright red draped cloth over the entrance'). Isolates the recolor to that object so the brass lamps, people and surroundings are untouched. Returns a maskURI. Not a hue/coordinate selection — a real object.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes hero + drape mask): keep the drape in the red family but deepen it toward maroon/wine — a small within-band hue nudge (well under ~60 deg, staying in red/wine; NOT a near-complementary rotation) together with a luminance drop that darkens the cloth, letting its existing luminosity carry the folds, sheen highlights and cast shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the lamps and people) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the fabric sheen) — both wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the drape lands on the deep-maroon house target instead of a still-bright candy red or a flat brick, still riding the original luminosity so the satin folds and shadow stay natural. A deepen-and-mute in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue.

Crop the recolored branch-4 hero to the 2:1 hero window with the grey card cropped OUT, at >=4320 x 2160 px — this maroon-drape version is what binds into the branch-4 banner (@Hero) and is also delivered as variant_b4_drape_maroon.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Branch-5 (level), badly OVER-exposed against a bright sky with blown pandal-roof highlights: PULL exposure/highlights/whites DOWN to recover the blown roof FIRST, then a small WB nudge so its grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Tonal recovery dominates here — a different problem from the cast frames. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 2:1 hero window at >=4320 x 2160 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

THE TRAP FRAME. Branch-6's frontage is genuinely DEEP-GOLD (real brass lamps + dense marigold) and it was shot under warm-but-NEUTRAL light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'cool the warm cast' correction used on frame 1, or 'cools an imagined blue cast', will neutralize the card OFF-neutral and strip the real festive gold the client is selling. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 2:1 hero window at >=4320 x 2160 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.
Branch-7 is tilted ~4 deg — level it before grading.

Strong cool BLUE open-shade cast AND dark: WARM strongly and lift shadows/exposure to bring it up while neutralizing its grey card to the shared white point; protect the frontage from going muddy. The biggest correction in the set — proof that identical batch numbers cannot serve every frame. Report the move. Frames 1-7 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 2:1 hero window at >=4320 x 2160 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Derive a traditional screen-print / halftone texture motif from a graded hero (branch-2's clean cropped frame) so the banner carries a printed-poster feel up close. No LPI parameter exists on this tool — it applies a fixed halftone screen. This is an agent-authored decorative motif, not a preset look.

Resize/crop the halftone motif to the banner's texture-panel window ratio (kept high-res so it prints crisp). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. This shared motif binds into every banner via @Texture. Deliverable.

Triage path A: the flat crest is solid two-colour line art, so it CAN honestly become clean vector. Prep-before-trace step 1: crop the oversized/off-centre export to the tight bounds of the emblem so the trace sees only the crest, not the white margin.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast and set the black/white points so the maroon and gold fills separate hard-edged from the white ground — a soft/aliased raster traces into ragged, doubled edges. (This crest sits on a WHITE ground, so its enclosed counters read as white after trace — a light-ground knockout, valid; no dark-ground counter claim.)

Trace the prepared flat crest into a clean SVG so it stays razor-sharp at the banner crest window across every branch. Tracing the RAW aliased export instead would produce a fuzzy, margin-bounded silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. Deliverable, bound via @Crest.

Triage path B DIVERGES: the foil seal is a PHOTOGRAPH of an embossed metallic surface — full of gradients and specular sheen — so it CANNOT become clean line art (vectorizing it would return a flat muddy silhouette and kill the foil). Crop only to the tight bounds of the seal; do NOT send it to image_vectorize.

Knock the dark surround to transparency so only the gold-foil seal remains, keeping every gradient, highlight and emboss shadow intact. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill, NOT a solid fill). This preserves the foil the vector path would have destroyed. It isolates the OUTER background only — no enclosed-interior knockout is claimed.

Square-crop/resize the transparent foil seal to the seal-window ratio at >=1296 px square so it prints sharp. Kept as a high-resolution RASTER placed via @Seal on every branch. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Deliverable — the triage-correct counterpart to brand_crest.svg.

Convert the supplied flattened proof PDF into a genuine editable .indd reuse source. Standalone deliverable — NOT used as the merge template (a convert_pdf_to_indd output has no live merge fields / image columns and would not bind); the merge runs against the separately hand-authored kanaka_mahal_banner_template.indd.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: hero_b1_final, hero_b2_final, hero_b3_final, hero_b4_final, hero_b5_final, hero_b6_final, hero_b7_final, brand_crest.svg, foil_seal_transparent.png, halftone_texture_motif.png
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the seven grey-card-neutralized hero crops plus the three shared marks (vector crest, transparent foil seal, halftone motif) so the merge can resolve them by the @Hero / @Crest / @Seal / @Texture columns. Files uploaded under the EXACT names the roster references (e.g. hero_b4_final.jpg for the branch-4 @Hero, brand_crest.svg for @Crest).
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @Hero (per-branch) and @Crest / @Seal / @Texture (shared) columns resolve to for each branch's single-record banner.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the seven roster rows (BranchName/Address/Phone/OfferLine/ValidDates) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve ALL FOUR image columns per row — drop that branch's graded hero into the @Hero window, the shared vectorized crest into @Crest, the transparent foil seal into @Seal, and the halftone motif into @Texture — producing EXACTLY ONE merged banner per row (seven banners); the auto-fit frames shrink long branch names. Binding the crest, seal, and motif through the shared image columns is what puts them on every banner — free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, so the merge is the only connector-doable path (this is what heals the killed design's empty-frame defect). [T] requires the hand-authored template with its four merge-wired image frames. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-record grid would not bind / cannot be produced.

Export the merged single-record banners to a press-ready CMYK PDF at the 12 ft x 6 ft design scale with 1-inch full-scale bleed, one banner per branch. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all seven banners, one page per branch) in a single call — it cannot export one named branch on its own, so no per-record named export is attempted. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 7; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Seven per-hero grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame in OPPOSITE directions: cool the warm-tungsten frame 1, warm the cool-LED frame 2, magenta-tint+lift the green/dark frame 3, modest neutralize on the mixed frame 4, tonally recover the overexposed frame 5, HOLD white balance on the genuinely-gold frame 6, strongly warm+lift the blue/dark frame 7) followed by an image_crop_and_resize that crops the grey card OUT, reframes to the 2:1 hero window and holds >=4320 x 2160 px, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 1/3/7 — every neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card so all seven converge on one shared white point. Branch-4's neutralized full-res frame (step 9, card still in frame) feeds BOTH the recolor branch and its final crop: image_select_by_prompt(10) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(11) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(12) -> crop(13), the two HSL passes both consuming drape_mask. Branch-2's graded crop (hero_b2_final, step 5) feeds the halftone motif: image_apply_halftone(21) -> crop_and_resize(22 -> halftone_texture_motif.png). The two brand marks TRIAGE into different paths: the flat crest runs crop_to_bounds(23) -> crisp adjustments(24) -> image_vectorize(25 -> brand_crest.svg), while the photographed foil seal diverges to crop_to_bounds(26) -> image_remove_background to transparency(27) -> crop_and_resize(28 -> foil_seal_transparent.png), deliberately never touching image_vectorize. Last year's proof back-converts once: document_convert_pdf(29 -> last_year_editable.indd). The seven final heroes plus the three shared marks converge into the upload session(30) -> finalize(31) -> document_merge_data_layout(32), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one merged banner per row, resolving @Hero (that branch's graded hero) plus the shared @Crest / @Seal / @Texture into the template's four merge-wired image frames. The merged set is exported once, by document_render_layout(33), to the single press-ready CMYK PDF carrying all seven banners (one page per branch); no per-record named export is attempted. Nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 33 connector calls, 14 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize/halftone/knockout, asset_* storage, document_* convert/merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps and the 3 auto_straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the seven neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision in a different direction (warm frame cooled, cool frame warmed, green/dark frame fixed on a second TINT axis, mixed frame modestly corrected, overexposed frame tonally recovered, genuinely-gold frame HELD on WB, blue/dark frame strongly warmed and lifted) all forced to converge on a single measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass, and every crop must additionally clear a numeric large-format print floor (>=4320 x 2160 px) reachable only by DOWNSCALE from the declared ~5400-6000 px camera sources. Layered on top are a masked luminosity-preserving drape recolor (a within-family bright-red -> deep-maroon deepen-and-mute executed as two image_adjust_hsl passes on a select_by_prompt object mask, an in-band adjacent shift the tool can actually hold — no near-complementary rotation, and with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong), an agent-authored halftone motif, a genuine two-way TRIAGE of the two superficially-similar brand marks (the flat crest prep-and-vectorized to clean line art; the photographed foil seal knocked to transparency and kept as raster, NOT traced), a PDF->.indd back-conversion, and a FOUR-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template that gives every produced asset a real bind path onto the banner. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout, no free-form placement; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT a merge target (the merge template is a supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; image_fill_area and image_apply_color_overlay are deliberately unused; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _vibrance_and_saturation / _brightness_and_contrast are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every branch hero carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and each neutralization is a divergent per-frame craft call toward one shared white point — the agent works by EYE and REPORTS the white-balance/exposure move and final pixel size it APPLIED (never a read pixel value), and the grader (which can measure) checks neutrality on the RETAINED card-bearing neutralized master of each frame; pushing identical batch numbers through seven differently-lit frames visibly leaves the series mismatched. A second, invisible-until-print failure gate is the two-way TRIAGE of the brand marks: the flat crest must be prepped-and-vectorized while the photographed gold-foil seal must be kept raster (transparency) — sending the foil through the same crop->vectorize path returns a flat muddy silhouette that passes as a thumbnail but prints dead across a 12-foot banner. A third checkable gate: the merged PDF page-count must equal the roster row-count (7), since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of seven differently-lit shots to a common measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction, plus a numeric large-format DPI floor (>=4320 x 2160 px, downscale-only) on every crop; (2) a masked, luminosity-preserving bright-red -> deep-maroon drape recolor (a within-family deepen-and-mute via the ONLY masked recolor path, image_adjust_hsl, on a real object mask — not color_overlay/fill_area) that keeps fabric folds and sheen natural; (3) the two-way brand-mark triage plus prep-before-trace discipline on the crest (crop-to-bounds -> crisp -> vectorize). TRAP THE BRIEF DOES NOT DISCLOSE: the brief never says WHICH branch is the genuinely-gold one, so a naive path batch-applies the 'cool the warm cast' correction to branch-6 (or cools an imagined blue cast), pushing its already-neutral card off-neutral and stripping the real festive gold the client is selling; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. (The mark triage is likewise undisclosed — the brief says 'prep both marks' without naming which cannot be traced.) MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, stated as decoupled claims so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (per-channel spread near zero) and one shared white point, evaluated on all seven RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (card still in frame), with the genuinely-gold branch's real colour preserved — never evaluated on a card-removed crop; (b) card-exclusion AND the >=4320 x 2160 px floor checked separately on the seven hero crops that bind; plus the agent reports per-frame WB/exposure params and final px, the drape recolored within its mask only, the crest a clean vector and the foil seal a sharp transparent-ground raster, and exactly one press-ready banner per roster row (page-count = 7).
